guard: A cancelled race arm whose in-flight effect lands is re-judged against the frontier: past it the pure tail is cut, before it the arm keeps running and can still win. A divergence raised inside a scope is never the scope's own outcome: the ladder rethrows it and settles nothing, a divergence among a race's settled arms unwinds the run ahead of the winner scan whichever arm won, and it cancels no sibling — a scope it passes through leaves every other arm to run to its own boundary, so a resume of the original source completes the run. (FAIL-FAST suite: markers are upstream of the cells they guard.)

mutations.name: the cut is never re-decided after an in-flight effect advances a cancelled arm
mutations.expectRed: the loser's infinite pure tail is abandoned once its in-flight effect lands past the frontier, and the run completes
mutations.completionMarker: ok and the resume takes the SAME path
mutations.cell: the loser's infinite pure tail is abandoned once its in-flight effect lands past the frontier, and the run completes
mutations.note: Without the listener the loser's verdict stays what the settle decided from its OLD clock, the infinite tail burns the step budget, and the run dies on L4013 after the race already settled ok. The suite is fail-fast, so the marker is the LAST line printed BEFORE the reddened cell (section 9's final cell): it proves the run reached the cell it is accused of reddening rather than dying earlier.

mutations.name: any landing on a cancelled arm cuts it, frontier ignored
mutations.expectRed: an arm whose in-flight effect lands BEFORE the frontier runs its pure tail and wins
mutations.completionMarker: ok the loser's infinite pure tail is abandoned once its in-flight effect lands past the frontier, and the run completes
mutations.cell: an arm whose in-flight effect lands BEFORE the frontier runs its pure tail and wins
mutations.note: The guard against over-cutting: an arm landing at 5000 against a frontier of 10000 can still win, and cutting it hands the race to the wrong arm. The cell asserts the early-landing arm WINS.

mutations.name: a divergence inside a scope settles as the scope's own L4000 failure (the defect)
mutations.expectRed: (1) and the scope entry stays PENDING rather than recording the divergence as its outcome
mutations.completionMarker: ok (1) a resume whose edit diverged inside the pending parallel throws the divergence
mutations.cell: (1) and the scope entry stays PENDING rather than recording the divergence as its outcome
mutations.note: Dropping the ladder entry puts the divergence through the generic settle (#1176): the scope is durably recorded `settled/failed` under `L4000` `scope-fault`, so the next resume replays a catchable `EffectError` instead of the divergence and the loudness is spent before anyone sees it. The first cell after the throw is the entry-shape cell, so the marker sits one cell UP: the suite is fail-fast and the fail happens AT this cell, so the marker proves the run reached it. Measured before the rule at 1498d82c9: settled/failed L4000, second resume EffectError(L4000).

mutations.name: a losing race arm's divergence is discarded by the winner scan (the defect)
mutations.find: (r.reason instanceof RunHeld || r.reason instanceof JournalAppendRejected || r.reason instanceof RunDivergence),
mutations.expectRed: (4) a divergence in a losing race arm surfaces as RunDivergence
mutations.completionMarker: ok (3) and no effect after the catch runs against the journal it diverged from
mutations.cell: (4) a divergence in a losing race arm surfaces as RunDivergence
mutations.note: Dropping `RunDivergence` from the hoist is exactly the pre-fix second site: the diverged arm is a rejected non-candidate, the scan picks the pure sibling, and the run COMPLETES with the winner's value while the run-level fault vanishes (measured at the base: outcome COMPLETED, logs [["win","pure","pure"]], race settled ok, the divergence never surfaced). The cell names the throw; the next cell holds the winner's value.

mutations.name: a divergence in a parallel arm cancels its sibling (the round-2 defect)
mutations.expectRed: (6) and the sibling arm's entry settles ok, not cancelled
mutations.completionMarker: ok (6) a divergence in one arm of a both-begun parallel still surfaces as RunDivergence
mutations.cell: (6) and the sibling arm's entry settles ok, not cancelled
mutations.note: Dropping `RunDivergence` from the `parallel` catch exemption restores the reviewer's failing input exactly: the divergence falls through the catch, every sibling is cancelled (`settled/cancelled` on the journal), and the ScopeFailed wrap is unwrapped by the ladder so the scope stays pending while the cancellation is already durable — a resume of the original source then threw Cancelled and settled the scope cancelled (measured on the seeded both-begun journal at f77b0b891). The fail-fast marker is the cell above: the run reached this cell before reddening.

mutations.name: a divergence in a fanOut branch cancels its sibling (the round-2 defect)
mutations.expectRed: (7) and the sibling branch's entry settles ok, not cancelled
mutations.completionMarker: ok (7) a divergence in one branch of a both-begun fanOut still surfaces as RunDivergence
mutations.cell: (7) and the sibling branch's entry settles ok, not cancelled
mutations.note: The `fanOut` catch holds the same host-side rule as `parallel`; dropping the divergence from it cancels the sibling branch durably (measured: sleep:w-y settled cancelled, original-source resume threw Cancelled, scope settled cancelled). Fail-fast marker is the cell above.

mutations.name: a diverging race arm stays a candidate and cancels the siblings (the round-2 defect)
mutations.find: e instanceof Cancelled || e instanceof RunReleased || e instanceof RunHeld || e instanceof JournalAppendRejected || e instanceof RunDivergence,
mutations.replace: e instanceof Cancelled || e instanceof RunReleased || e instanceof RunHeld || e instanceof JournalAppendRejected,
mutations.expectRed: (8) and the other arm's entry settles ok, not cancelled
mutations.completionMarker: ok (8) a divergence in one arm of a both-begun race still surfaces as RunDivergence
mutations.cell: (8) and the other arm's entry settles ok, not cancelled
mutations.note: The first round added the divergence to the hoist above the winner scan, which surfaces it; without the non-candidacy the diverging arm still settles as a candidate in `onSettle` and cancels its siblings before the hoist throws (measured on the seeded journal at f77b0b891: slow-work settled cancelled even though the hoist still threw the divergence). Both halves are needed: the hoist surfaces it, the non-candidacy keeps it from cancelling. Fail-fast marker is the cell above.
